<!--
Combines the three "merge into core pipeline" covariates -- elevation,
wind, and slope -- into one file, matching the categorization decided
earlier this session: elevation/slope/wind/tidal merge into the
tiering pipeline, veg and storm periods stay separate (see
thesis_veg.qmd / usgs_veg.qmd's own notes on why). Tidal isn't built
yet -- picking that up in the next session, per your own plan. This
file is meant to eventually replace elev_z_flux.csv as
master_analysis_flagtier.qmd's input; that swap isn't made here (see
closing note), since it's a real pipeline change worth doing
deliberately, not as a side effect of this file existing.

JOIN GRANULARITY, WORTH BEING EXPLICIT ABOUT: elevation and wind are
already present in elev_z_wind_flux.csv at the Site+Tran+Dist+
Replicate level (elevation was surveyed per replicate position; wind
is a per-deployment-window value broadcast across whatever rows share
that window). Slope is NOT replicate-specific -- it's a property of
the transect line at a given distance, from the dense along-transect
survey, independent of which individual replicate sits there. So the
join below is Site+Tran+Dist (3 keys, no Replicate) for slope, even
though the base table already has a Replicate column -- every
replicate at a given point gets the same local_slope value, same
broadcast logic as the USGS elevation/veg joins.

COVERAGE INHERITED FROM UPSTREAM, NOT NEW HERE: slope only exists for
GiantMarsh and CorteMadera's rebased range -- SanPablo and
Buck'sLanding coverage was completed this session (see
thesis_slope.qmd), so all 4 sites should now have slope, but the
extrapolated flag and the accepted Buck'sLanding/SanPablo near-edge
noise both carry through unchanged, not re-decided here. Wind only
covers the July 2025-June 2026 campaign -- July 2022-June 2023 rows
will have NA wind metrics, inherited from elev_z_wind_flux.csv.
-->

```{r, load packages}
source("C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\code\\R\\setup.R")
```

```{r, load elevation+wind and slope}
elev_z_wind_flux <- readr::read_csv("C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\data\\elev_z_wind_flux.csv")

local_slope_thesis <- readr::read_csv("C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\data\\local_slope_thesis.csv")
```

```{r, key both sides consistently before joining}
elev_z_wind_flux_keyed <- elev_z_wind_flux |>
  mutate(
    Site = str_squish(as.character(Site)),
    Tran = str_squish(as.character(Tran)),
    Dist = as.numeric(as.character(Dist))
  )

local_slope_keyed <- local_slope_thesis |>
  mutate(
    Site = str_squish(as.character(Site)),
    Tran = str_squish(as.character(Tran)),
    Dist = as.numeric(as.character(Dist))
  ) |>
  select(Site, Tran, Dist, local_slope, fitted_elevation_m, extrapolated) |>
  rename(slope_fitted_elevation_m = fitted_elevation_m)   # avoid colliding with the base table's own Elevation_m
```

```{r, join -- broadcast slope across replicates, same pattern as USGS elevation/veg}
elev_z_wind_slope_flux <- elev_z_wind_flux_keyed |>
  left_join(local_slope_keyed, by = c("Site", "Tran", "Dist"))

readr::write_csv(elev_z_wind_slope_flux, "C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\data\\elev_z_wind_slope_flux.csv")

nrow(elev_z_wind_slope_flux) == nrow(elev_z_wind_flux)   # confirms no fan-out or row loss from this join
```

```{r, coverage diagnostics -- confirms what's present, fixes nothing}
# How many rows have each covariate, and how many have all three --
# expected to be less than 100% for slope (SanPablo/Buck'sLanding
# coverage just added, worth confirming it actually joined) and for
# wind (2022-2023 rows will show FALSE).
elev_z_wind_slope_flux |>
  summarise(
    n_total = n(),
    has_elevation = sum(!is.na(Elevation_m)),
    has_wind = sum(!is.na(mean_wind_speed_kt)),
    has_slope = sum(!is.na(local_slope)),
    has_all_three = sum(!is.na(Elevation_m) & !is.na(mean_wind_speed_kt) & !is.na(local_slope))
  )

# Breakdown by Site -- confirms slope coverage reaches all 4 sites now,
# not just the 2 that had topo data earlier this session.
elev_z_wind_slope_flux |>
  group_by(Site) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    has_slope = sum(!is.na(local_slope)),
    has_wind = sum(!is.na(mean_wind_speed_kt)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```
